ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, $BD\perp AC$ at point $D$, $AC=10$, $\cos C=\frac{3}{5}$, then how long is $CD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $BD\perp AC$ and $\angle ABC=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\cos C=\frac{CD}{BC}=\frac{BC}{AC}=\frac{3}{5}$, \\
given that $AC=10$, \\
it follows that $BC=6$, \\
hence, $CD=\frac{3}{5}BC=\boxed{\frac{18}{5}}$

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, B, C form a triangle with D lying on side AC, and segment BD is drawn from B to AC as an altitude, so triangle BCD is a smaller right triangle sharing angle C with the large triangle. From the text, use that angle ABC is 90°, BD ⟂ AC, AC = 10, and cos C = 3/5. In the large right triangle ABC, AC is the hypotenuse and BC is adjacent to angle C, so cos C = BC/AC = 3/5, giving BC = 6. Then in right triangle BCD, with hypotenuse BC and adjacent leg CD to angle C, cos C = CD/BC = 3/5, so CD = (3/5)·6 = 18/5.
